descriptionChirho: Feminine noun עֹפֶרֶת designating the heavy metal lead, used in descriptions of metallurgical processes (Num 31:22; Ezek 22:18, 20; 27:12), in Job's famous wish for permanent inscription (Job 19:24), in Zechariah's prophetic vision of the lead cover on the ephah (Zech 5:7-8), and in the Song of the Sea simile (Exod 15:10). All three clusters represent the same metal in different syntactic positions: conjunction-prefixed 'and lead' (S123002), standalone or with article 'the lead / lead' (S123003), and comparative 'like the lead' (S123006). Multilingual evidence uniformly identifies one substance: Spanish 'plomo,' Hindi 'सीसा / सीसे,' Arabic 'رَصَاص,' Korean '납,' Swahili 'risasi.' The simile usage in Exodus 15:10 is figurative but the referent remains the literal metal.
